rule-snelheid-bebouwd.question: What is the general maximum speed within built-up areas in Flanders, unless otherwise indicated?
options: 50 km/h
30 km/h
70 km/h
90 km/h
rule-snelheid-bebouwd.explanation: In Flanders and Wallonia, the standard speed limit within built-up areas is 50 km/h (art. 11.1). In the Brussels Capital Region, on the other hand, the standard speed is 30 km/h.

rule-snelheid-buiten-vl.question: What is the standard maximum speed outside built-up areas on Flemish roads since the speed reform, unless otherwise indicated?
options: 50 km/h
70 km/h
90 km/h
120 km/h
rule-snelheid-buiten-vl.explanation: In Flanders and Brussels, the standard speed limit outside built-up areas is 70 km/h (art. 11.2). Only in the Walloon Region is the standard still 90 km/h.

rule-snelheid-autosnelweg.question: What is the speed limit on motorways in Belgium?
options: 100 km/h
110 km/h
120 km/h
130 km/h
rule-snelheid-autosnelweg.explanation: According to Article 11.2.1°a, a maximum speed of 120 km/h applies on Belgian motorways, unless a traffic sign imposes a different speed.

rule-snelheid-min-autosnelweg.question: What minimum speed generally applies on a motorway, if circumstances permit?
options: 50 km/h
60 km/h
80 km/h
70 km/h
rule-snelheid-min-autosnelweg.explanation: According to Article 21.2, a minimum speed of 70 km/h applies on motorways, except when circumstances such as traffic jams prevent this.

rule-alcohol-algemeen.question: What is the legal alcohol limit for a regular driver in Belgium?
options: 0.5 per mille
0.0 per mille
0.2 per mille
0.8 per mille
rule-alcohol-algemeen.explanation: For regular drivers, the legal alcohol limit is 0.5 per mille in the blood (0.22 mg/l of exhaled air, Article 34 of the Road Traffic Act).

rule-alcohol-beroep.question: Which stricter alcohol limit applies in Belgium to professional drivers, such as bus, taxi and truck drivers?
options: 0.0 per mille
0.2 per mille
0.5 per mille
0.35 per mille
rule-alcohol-beroep.explanation: Professional drivers must comply with 0.2 per mille (0.09 mg/l of exhaled air) according to Article 34 of the Road Traffic Act.

rule-gordel-algemeen.question: Do you have to wear a seat belt in the back seat of a car?
options: No, only in the front is mandatory
Only mandatory outside built-up areas
Yes, on every seat equipped with a belt
Only compulsory for children
rule-gordel-algemeen.explanation: According to Article 35.1.1, seat belts are mandatory in the front and rear, on every seat that is equipped with a seat belt.

rule-kinderzitje.question: Up to what height is a child required to use an approved child restraint system in the car?
options: Up to the age of 12, regardless of height
rule-kinderzitje.explanation: According to Article 35.1.1, children under the age of 18 and shorter than 1.35 m must be transported in a child restraint system suitable for them.

rule-gsm.question: As a driver, are you allowed to hold your mobile phone in your hand while stopped at a red traffic light?
options: No, holding on is only allowed when the vehicle is stationary or parked
Yes, because the car is stationary
Yes, as long as you don't call
No, but only on motorways
rule-gsm.explanation: Waiting at a red light does not count as standing still or parking (art. 2.22 and 2.23). Article 8.4 prohibits holding or manipulating mobile devices with a screen while driving; the engine does not legally have to be switched off.

rule-voorrang-rechts.question: Who has priority at an intersection where priority is not specifically regulated?
options: Traffic from the left
Traffic from the right
The largest vehicle
Whoever arrives first
rule-voorrang-rechts.explanation: Without indications, the right-of-way rule applies, as determined in Article 12.3.1 of the Highway Code.

rule-voorrang-rechts-gestopt.question: Do you lose your priority from the right if you stop briefly at the intersection before continuing?
options: Yes, anyone who stops loses priority
Only if a stop order applies
No, a stopped driver from the right also retains priority
Only outside built-up areas
rule-voorrang-rechts-gestopt.explanation: According to settled case law in Article 12.3.1, a driver from the right retains priority, even if he first stops before the intersection.

rule-rotonde.question: Who has priority at a roundabout indicated by sign D5?
options: The traffic that wants to enter the roundabout
Always traffic from the right
The largest vehicle
The traffic already on the roundabout
rule-rotonde.explanation: At a roundabout indicated by sign D5, traffic already on it has priority over those who want to join (art. 12.3.1).
rule-rotonde.signExplanation: Sign D5 indicates a roundabout where traffic must drive in the indicated direction. Drivers on the roundabout have priority over approaching traffic that wants to enter (art. 12.3.1 and art. 68.3 of the Highway Code).

rule-prioritair.question: What should you do if a priority vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches?
options: Immediately make way and give way
Just continue on your way
Only move aside when you are at an intersection
Speed up to clear the intersection
rule-prioritair.explanation: As soon as the audible horn of a priority vehicle sounds, every road user must immediately give way and give way (art. 38).

rule-fietser-inhalen.question: What minimum lateral distance should you keep when overtaking a cyclist outside built-up areas?
options: 1 meter
1.5 meters
0.5 meters
2 meters
rule-fietser-inhalen.explanation: According to Article 40ter, at least 1.5 meters lateral distance is mandatory outside built-up areas; within built-up areas this is 1 meter.

rule-zebra.question: What should you do if a pedestrian is crossing at a zebra crossing?
options: Have priority, because you are in the car
Drive past quickly before reaching the road
Give way and stop if necessary
Only grant priority outside built-up areas
rule-zebra.explanation: According to Article 40.4.2, a driver must give way and, if necessary, stop for pedestrians crossing at a crossing.

rule-fietser-aan-hand.question: How is a cyclist treated who crosses a zebra crossing while holding his bicycle?
options: As a cyclist, so without priority
He is not allowed to cross at a zebra crossing
Only as a pedestrian if he also wears a bicycle helmet
As a pedestrian, so with priority
rule-fietser-aan-hand.explanation: Anyone who carries his bicycle by hand is treated as a pedestrian (art. 2.46) and has priority on the zebra crossing (art. 40.4.2).

rule-verzekering.question: What is legally required for every motor vehicle driving on public roads in Belgium?
options: Civil liability insurance (BA/WAM)
Only a valid inspection
Only comprehensive insurance
Insurance is not mandatory if you are properly insured through your health insurance
rule-verzekering.explanation: The WAM law (art. 2) obliges every motor vehicle that drives on public roads to have civil liability insurance.

rule-reddingsstrook.question: What should you do if traffic on a motorway with at least two lanes in each direction comes to a standstill or moves at a walking pace?
options: Drive on the hard shoulder
Create a rescue lane between the left and other lanes
Just stay in your lane
Form a rescue lane, but only if you see a flashing light
rule-reddingsstrook.explanation: According to Articles 9.8 and 2.70, drivers must always form a rescue lane during traffic jams on roads with at least two lanes in each direction.

rule-mistlichten.question: When are the rear fog lights of a car required to be on?
options: Always in the rain, even light rain
Always at night
In fog or snowfall with less than 100 m visibility, or in heavy rain
Only on motorways
rule-mistlichten.explanation: According to article 30.1.2°, rear fog lights are mandatory in fog or snowfall that limits visibility to less than 100 m, and in heavy rain. Use is prohibited in all other circumstances.

rule-rijbewijs-begeleider.question: From what age can you obtain a provisional driving license B with companion in Belgium?
options: 16 years old
18 years old
19 years old
17 years old
rule-rijbewijs-begeleider.explanation: With a supervisor you can obtain a provisional driving license B from the age of 17 (after the theory exam); without a supervisor only from the age of 18, after 20 hours of practical lessons (Royal Decree of 10 July 2006, art. 2-4).

rule-begeleider-ervaring.question: How many years must a supervisor have had his driving license at least to act as a supervisor with a provisional driving license B?
options: 8 years
3 years
5 years
10 years
rule-begeleider-ervaring.explanation: A supervisor must have held a valid driving license B for at least 8 years at the time of the training (Royal Decree of 10 July 2006, art. 3, § 2, b).

rule-overweg.question: What should you do when you approach a level crossing and the red lights start flashing?
options: Cross as quickly as possible before the barriers lower
Stop and wait for the lights to stop flashing
Just slow down, don't stop
Only stop when you see the barriers lowering
rule-overweg.explanation: As soon as the red lights flash, it is prohibited according to Article 20.3, 2° to drive onto the level crossing, even if the barriers are still open.

rule-zone30.question: What speed limit applies in a zone 30?
options: 20 km/h
40 km/h
30 km/h
50 km/h
rule-zone30.explanation: In a zone 30, according to Article 22quater and 65.5, you may not drive faster than 30 km/h.

rule-estep-helm-2026.question: From what construction speed is a crash helmet mandatory on a motorized propulsion device (such as an e-scooter)?
options: Above 20 km/h
Above 15 km/h
Above 25 km/h
A helmet is never mandatory on an e-scooter
rule-estep-helm-2026.explanation: According to Article 36 of the Highway Code (introduced by the Royal Decree of August 27, 2026, effective September 1, 2026), a crash helmet is mandatory on motorized propulsion equipment with a construction speed of more than 20 km/h.

rule-vierwieler-helm-2024.question: Must the driver of an agricultural vehicle that is legally considered a "four-wheeler with motor" wear a crash helmet?
options: Yes, always, regardless of construction speed or steering type
No, if the construction speed does not exceed 40 km/h and the vehicle does not have a motorcycle-like handlebar
Only if there is no seat belt
Only mandatory outside built-up areas
rule-vierwieler-helm-2024.explanation: Article 36, first paragraph, excludes agricultural vehicles that qualify as four-wheelers with a motor from the crash helmet requirement, provided that their construction speed does not exceed 40 km/h and they do not have a handlebar like a motorcycle (Royal Decree of 2 October 2023). Quads with motorcycle handlebars remain mandatory to wear helmets.

rule-middenrijbaan-2022.question: Where should you drive on a road that has a center lane (two parallel imaginary edges of two short white stripes each)?
options: You drive in the central center lane and swerve to the side lane to cross or overtake oncoming traffic
You must always drive in the right side lane and may never enter the center lane
The center lane is reserved exclusively for buses and priority vehicles
You may only use the center lane to turn left
rule-middenrijbaan-2022.explanation: A central carriageway (art. 2.71) functions as the carriageway for motor vehicles; drivers follow them (art. 9.1.1) and may only swerve to the side lane (art. 2.72) to cross (art. 15.3) or overtake (art. 16.5).

rule-estep-leeftijd-2022.question: From what minimum age are you allowed to drive a motorized propulsion device (such as an e-scooter) on public roads in Belgium?
options: Vanaf 12 jaar
Vanaf 14 jaar
From 16 years (except in residential areas, play streets or pedestrian zones)
Vanaf 18 jaar
rule-estep-leeftijd-2022.explanation: Article 8.2, 7° sets the minimum age for driving a motorized vehicle at 16 years, except in residential areas, yards, play streets or pedestrian zones.

rule-estep-passagier-2022.question: Can two people ride on one electric scooter on public roads?
options: Yes, if both wear helmets
Yes, provided the total weight remains below 120 kg
No, it is expressly prohibited to transport passengers on a propellant device
Only if the passenger is a child under 7 years old
rule-estep-passagier-2022.explanation: Article 44.2 expressly prohibits the carriage of passengers on propellant aircraft, except on aircraft specifically built for passenger transport.

rule-speed-pedelec-d9-2022.question: Is a speed pedelec driver allowed to use a part of the public road indicated by sign D9 (pedestrians, cyclists and mopeds class A)?
options: No, speed pedelecs are never allowed on a D9 path
Yes, speed pedelecs are allowed to use the D9 path, unless a sign prohibits them from doing so
Only if they do not drive faster than 15 km/h
Only outside built-up areas
rule-speed-pedelec-d9-2022.explanation: By the Royal Decree of July 30, 2022 (in effect on October 1, 2022, art. 9.1.2° and 69.3), the permission for drivers of speed pedelecs on the D9 path was restored, unless a sign denies them access.

rule-velomobiel-2022.question: What additional visibility requirement applies to a velomobile (closed recumbent bicycle) with a height of less than 1 meter?
options: An orange flashing light on the roof
A yellow or orange reflective strip on the sides
Mandatory yellow side indicators
A fluorescent body coat around the entire vehicle
rule-velomobiel-2022.explanation: According to article 82.1.2, 6°, velomobiles must always be equipped with a yellow or orange reflective strip on the sides.

rule-fietsstraat-f111-2021.question: How far do the specific traffic rules of a cycling zone (indicated by sign F111) apply?
options: Until the next intersection, unless the sign is repeated
Until the traffic sign F113 that indicates the end of the cycling zone; a cycling zone can include several streets
Always over a fixed distance of 250 meters
Only at the first 50 meters
rule-fietsstraat-f111-2021.explanation: Since the Royal Decree of March 12, 2023, a "cycling street" has been called a "cycling zone" (art. 2.61): it can include several public roads and runs to the traffic sign F113, not automatically to the next intersection.

30 km/h
20 km/h

rule-estep-trottoir-2022.question: Can you ride a motorized e-scooter on the sidewalk?
options: No, e-scooters follow the rules for cyclists and should never be ridden on the sidewalk (unless you walk them by the hand)
Yes, as long as you don't drive faster than 6 km/h
Yes, but only if there is no cycle path
Yes, but only within built-up areas
rule-estep-trottoir-2022.explanation: Since July 1, 2022 (Act May 15, 2022, art. 3, which amends art. 7bis), drivers of motorized propulsion equipment are equated with cyclists. They are no longer allowed to drive on the sidewalk, regardless of their speed.

rule-estep-snelheid-2022.question: What is the maximum construction speed of a motorized propulsion device (such as an e-scooter) to be allowed to drive on public roads?
options: 18 km/h
25 km/h
30 km/h
45 km/h
rule-estep-snelheid-2022.explanation: According to Article 2.15.2 of the Highway Code, the maximum speed due to the design of a motorized propulsion device is a maximum of 25 km/h.

rule-estep-parkeren-2022.question: Where can you leave an electric shared scooter after your ride?
options: Random on the sidewalk, as long as it's flat on the ground
In the middle of the cycle path
Outside the road and parking lanes, without hindering or endangering other road users
Only in paid car parks
rule-estep-parkeren-2022.explanation: Article 23.3 requires that propulsion devices such as e-scooters be positioned outside the roadway and parking lanes, without hindering or endangering other road users. Specific drop zones are a municipal regulation, not a federal highway code rule.

rule-gsm-houder-2022.question: Under what conditions is a driver allowed to use a smartphone for navigation while driving?
options: As long as the device is on the driver's lap
When the driver holds the device with one hand
As long as the speaker is at maximum volume
Only when the device is attached to the vehicle in a specially intended holder
rule-gsm-houder-2022.explanation: Article 8.4 of the Highway Code prohibits the use, holding or manipulation of a mobile device with a screen, unless it is attached to the vehicle in a suitable holder.

rule-speed-pedelec-rijbewijs-2022.question: What minimum driving license do you need to drive a speed pedelec on public roads?
options: At least a category AM driving license (moped) or category B (car)
No driver's license is required
Mandatory motorcycle license category A
Only a special bicycle certificate from the municipality
rule-speed-pedelec-rijbewijs-2022.explanation: A speed pedelec is categorized as a class P moped. The driver must be at least 16 years old and have at least an AM driving license or a car driving license B.

rule-speed-pedelec-snelheid-2022.question: Up to what maximum speed may the pedal assistance of a speed pedelec legally remain active?
options: 25 km/h
45 km/h
35 km/h
50 km/h
rule-speed-pedelec-snelheid-2022.explanation: According to Article 2.17 of the Highway Code, a speed pedelec provides pedal assistance up to a maximum of 45 km/h. Above that speed, the auxiliary engine must switch off automatically.

rule-velomobiel-hoogte-2022.question: Where on a velomobile should the mandatory reflective strip be placed?
options: On the sides
Front only
Rear only
On the roof
rule-velomobiel-hoogte-2022.explanation: Article 82.1.2, 6° prescribes that velomobiles must have a yellow or orange reflective strip on their sides.

rule-reddingsstrook-vorming-2022.question: How are drivers supposed to form a rescue lane on a road with three lanes in the same direction in the event of a traffic jam?
options: All cars must immediately swerve to the emergency lane
Vehicles in the middle lane must stop and turn off their engines
The two right lanes deviate to the left and the left lane to the right
The leftmost lane deviates as much as possible to the left, the other two lanes deviate as much as possible to the right
rule-reddingsstrook-vorming-2022.explanation: According to Articles 9.8 and 2.70, drivers in the far left lane must swerve as much as possible to the left and drivers in the other lanes to the right, so that there is free passage between them.

rule-ritsen-locatie.question: Where should you merge in slowed down traffic during a lane reduction (zipping)?
options: Just before the narrowing of the lane
At least 500 meters before the narrowing
As soon as you see the first road works announcement board
On the emergency lane to move forward more quickly
rule-ritsen-locatie.explanation: According to Article 12bis, drivers must continue driving in very slow traffic until just before the narrowing and only merge there.

rule-ritsen-voorrang.question: How does priority work with mandatory zipping at the point of narrowing?
options: Drivers in the main lane always have priority and do not have to let anyone in between
Drivers in the free lane must alternately give way to one merging driver
Whoever accelerates fastest has priority
Only trucks must give way to cars
rule-ritsen-voorrang.explanation: Article 12bis stipulates that drivers in the free lane at the narrowing point must alternately give way to one merging vehicle.

rule-fietsstraat-inhalen.question: Can a car overtake a cyclist in a bicycle street?
options: Yes, if there is at least 1 meter between them
Yes, if the cyclist drives slower than 15 km/h
No, motor vehicles are never allowed to overtake cyclists in a bicycle street
Only if the cyclist expressly gives a hand gesture
rule-fietsstraat-inhalen.explanation: In a bicycle street (art. 22novies) it is prohibited for motor vehicles to overtake cyclists at all times.

rule-fietsstraat-snelheid.question: What is the absolute maximum speed for all traffic in a bicycle street?
options: 15 km/h
20 km/h
25 km/h
30 km/h
rule-fietsstraat-snelheid.explanation: According to Article 22novies, the speed in a bicycle street may never exceed 30 km/h, neither for cars nor for cyclists.

rule-fietser-b22.question: What does this permission sign (B22) allow for cyclists and drivers of speed pedelecs at a red traffic light?
options: Cyclists may turn right at red lights, provided they give priority to other traffic and pedestrians
Cyclists must stop until the light turns green
Cyclists are automatically given absolute priority over crossing traffic when turning
All motorized vehicles are also allowed to turn right on red
rule-fietser-b22.explanation: Traffic sign B22 allows cyclists and speed pedelecs to continue and turn right at red or orange-yellow lights, provided they give way (art. 67.3).
rule-fietser-b22.signTitle: Permission for cyclists to turn right at a red light
rule-fietser-b22.signExplanation: Traffic sign B22 allows cyclists and drivers of speed pedelecs to turn right at a red or orange-yellow traffic light, provided they give priority to other traffic and crossing pedestrians (art. 67.3 of the Highway Code).

rule-fietser-b23.question: What does this permission sign (B23) mean for cyclists and drivers of speed pedelecs at a red traffic light?
options: Cyclists have to wait until it turns green before they can continue straight
Cyclists may ride straight through a red light, provided they give way to other traffic and pedestrians
Cyclists may turn left without stopping
The red light is defective and disabled
rule-fietser-b23.explanation: Sign B23 allows cyclists and drivers of speed pedelecs to drive straight ahead at a red or orange-yellow light, provided they give way (art. 67.3).
rule-fietser-b23.signTitle: Permission for cyclists to drive straight through at red lights
rule-fietser-b23.signExplanation: Traffic sign B23 allows cyclists and drivers of speed pedelecs to drive straight ahead at a red or orange-yellow traffic light, provided they give priority to other traffic and crossing pedestrians (art. 67.3 of the Highway Code).

rule-voorrang-aardeweg.question: Does a driver coming from the right on a dirt road have priority over a driver on a public road with a carriageway?
options: Yes, priority from the right applies always and everywhere
Only if the driver is driving an agricultural vehicle on the dirt road
No, anyone coming from a dirt road or a path onto a public road with a carriageway must give way
Only if the road is narrower than 3 meters
rule-voorrang-aardeweg.explanation: According to Article 12.3.1, b), every driver must give way when coming from an earth road or a path onto a public road with a carriageway.

rule-voorrang-uitrit.question: Who has priority when a driver leaves a garage, parking lot or private property onto a public road?
options: The driver coming out of the garage, coming from the right
The driver who leaves the garage, provided he blows the horn
Pedestrians have to wait, but vehicles have priority
Road users on public roads; the exiting driver performs a maneuver and must give priority to everyone
rule-voorrang-uitrit.explanation: Driving onto a public road from a property or parking lot is, according to Article 12.4, a maneuver in which priority must be given to all other road users.

rule-voorrang-afslaan-tegenligger.question: You turn left at a similar intersection. Do you have to give priority to an oncoming car that wants to drive straight ahead?
options: Yes, anyone turning left must give priority to oncoming traffic going straight ahead or turning right
No, because whoever turns left has priority from the right compared to the oncoming vehicle
Only if the oncoming vehicle is already stopped at the intersection
Only within built-up areas
rule-voorrang-afslaan-tegenligger.explanation: According to article 19.3.3°, the driver turning to the left must give priority to oncoming traffic on the carriageway he is about to leave.

rule-voorrang-tram-algemeen.question: Does the general right-of-way priority apply to a tram at an intersection without traffic signs or traffic lights?
options: Yes, a tram must always give priority to cars from the right
No, a tram has priority over all other road users, both from the left and from the right
Only if the tram comes from the left
Only if the tram has passengers on board
rule-voorrang-tram-algemeen.explanation: According to Articles 12.1 and 12.3.1, rail vehicles (trams) always have priority over other road users, unless otherwise arranged by traffic lights or authorized persons.

rule-voorrang-tram-voetganger.question: Should a tram stop for a pedestrian crossing on a zebra crossing without traffic lights?
options: Yes, pedestrians on a zebra crossing always have absolute priority over all vehicles including trams
Only if the pedestrian is a child or elderly person
No, the tram retains its right of way and does not have to stop for pedestrians crossing
Only at night when the tram has lights on
rule-voorrang-tram-voetganger.explanation: According to Article 12.1, every road user, including a crossing pedestrian, must give priority to rail vehicles such as the tram.

rule-bus-bebouwde-kom.question: What should you do if a scheduled bus wants to leave its stop within a built-up area with flashing lights?
options: Sound the horn and drive past quickly before the bus leaves
Always overtake on the left side
Just keep your speed; the bus has to wait
Slow down and stop if necessary to give the bus priority to leave the stop
rule-bus-bebouwde-kom.explanation: Within built-up areas, according to Article 39, you must slow down and, if necessary, stop to give a bus that turns on its direction indicator the opportunity to leave its stop.

rule-bus-buiten-bebouwde-kom.question: Do you have to stop outside the built-up area for a scheduled bus that wants to drive away from a bus stop with its direction indicator?
options: No, the obligation to give priority to a driving bus only applies within built-up areas
Yes, this rule applies everywhere on public roads
Yes, but only on roads with a speed limit of 70 km/h
Only when the bus driver waves his hand
rule-bus-buiten-bebouwde-kom.explanation: Article 39 obliges drivers to give way to a bus driving away only within built-up areas. Outside built-up areas, the bus driver must give priority before driving onto the road.

rule-manoeuvre-achteruitrijden.question: Who has priority when you reverse out of a street or parking space?
options: You, when you're already on the road with half the car
All other road users; Reversing is a maneuver where you must give priority to everyone
You have priority over cyclists and pedestrians
The priority of the right continues to apply
rule-manoeuvre-achteruitrijden.explanation: Reversing is a maneuver according to article 12.4. The driver performing a maneuver must give priority to all other road users.

rule-manoeuvre-rijstrookwissel.question: What are the rules when changing lanes on a multi-lane road (other than a zipper situation)?
options: As soon as you turn on your turn signal, drivers behind you in the lane in front of you must brake
You may only change if there is no other vehicle in sight within 500 meters
You are performing a maneuver and must give way to the drivers in the lane you are going to
Drivers in the left lane always have priority over drivers in the right lane
rule-manoeuvre-rijstrookwissel.explanation: Changing lanes is a maneuver (art. 12.4). You must turn on your turn signal in time and give priority to traffic in the target lane.

rule-oversteekplaats-fietser.question: Does a cyclist at a bicycle crossing (indicated by white blocks) automatically have priority over approaching cars on the road?
options: Yes, just like pedestrians on a zebra crossing, cyclists crossing the road always have priority
Only if the cyclist comes from the right
Only if the cyclist cycles faster than 20 km/h
No, cyclists at a crossing must give way to approaching traffic on the roadway (unless traffic lights are green)
rule-oversteekplaats-fietser.explanation: According to Article 40ter, cyclists do not have priority at a crossing bicycle crossing. They may only enter the crossing with caution, taking into account approaching traffic.

rule-fietser-op-zebrapad.question: Does a cyclist who cycles across a zebra crossing have the same priority as a pedestrian?
options: No, only those who dismount and walk with their bicycle in their hands are considered pedestrians and have priority
Yes, every cyclist on a zebra crossing has priority
Yes, provided he does not drive faster than 10 km/h
Only if there is no cycle path nearby
rule-fietser-op-zebrapad.explanation: A cyclist who remains seated on his bicycle at a zebra crossing does not have pedestrian priority (art. 40.4.2°). Only when he gets off and goes on foot does he have priority as a pedestrian.

rule-parkeren-zebrapad-afstand.question: At what minimum distance before a pedestrian crossing is stopping and parking on the road prohibited?
options: At least 10 meters
At least 5 meters
At least 3 meters
At least 15 meters
rule-parkeren-zebrapad-afstand.explanation: Article 24.4° prohibits standing and parking at the crossing and on the roadway within a distance of 5 meters in front of the crossing.

rule-parkeren-bushalte-afstand.question: Within what distance on either side of a bus stop sign is parking prohibited if there are no road markings?
options: 5 meters on either side
10 meters on either side
15 meters on either side of the board
25 meters on either side
rule-parkeren-bushalte-afstand.explanation: According to article 25.1.2°, parking is prohibited less than 15 meters on either side of the sign indicating a bus or tram stop.

rule-stilstaan-vs-parkeren.question: According to the highway code, what is the strict difference between standing still and parking?
options: Standing still is when the engine is running; when the engine is off it is always parking
Standing still may last a maximum of 15 minutes regardless of the activity
There is no legal difference between standing still and parking
Standing still is only the time needed to allow people to get in or out or to load or unload goods; everything else is parking
rule-stilstaan-vs-parkeren.explanation: According to Articles 2.22 and 2.23, standing still is limited to the time necessary for the boarding or disembarking of persons or the loading and unloading of goods. Any other standing still legally counts as parking.

rule-parkeren-kruispunt-afstand.question: Within what distance from an intersection is it prohibited to park a vehicle on the road?
options: Less than 5 meters from the extension of the outer edge of the transverse carriageway
Less than 2 meters from the intersection
Less than 10 meters from the intersection
Parking at an intersection is only prohibited if there is a yellow cross
rule-parkeren-kruispunt-afstand.explanation: Article 24, 7° prohibits standing or parking less than 5 meters from the extension of the nearest edge of the transverse carriageway of an intersection.

rule-parkeren-brandkraan.question: At what minimum distance in front of or behind another stationary or parked vehicle are you not allowed to park?
options: Less than 30 centimeters
Less than 1 meter
Less than 3 meters
There is no minimum distance as long as you don't collide
rule-parkeren-brandkraan.explanation: Article 25.1, 1° prohibits parking less than 1 meter in front of or behind another stationary or parked vehicle, and anywhere where the entry or exit of another vehicle would be impeded.

rule-verlichting-tunnels.question: Which lights must be on when you enter a lighted tunnel during the day?
options: The four direction indicators
Only the parking lights are sufficient
The dipped beams (or main beams) must be on, even in a lit tunnel
No lighting whatsoever when the tunnel is lit
rule-verlichting-tunnels.explanation: A tunnel rarely offers more than 200 meters of clear visibility, even during the day; As a result, the general obligation of Article 30.1 to use the dipped beams (or high beams) applies. The highway code does not mention tunnels separately, but that visibility criterion almost always applies in practice.

rule-verlichting-duisternis.question: From what point onwards must visibility be reduced during the day due to fog, snow or rain, at least the dipped beam headlights must be switched on?
options: Visibility from less than 500 meters
Visibility from less than 300 meters
Only when you can see less than 50 meters away
Once visibility is reduced to less than approximately 200 metres
rule-verlichting-duisternis.explanation: Article 30.1 requires the use of dipped beam headlights (or high beam headlights) between dusk and dawn, and during the day when visibility is less than approximately 200 meters.

rule-grootlicht-tegenligger.question: What should you do with your high beams when an oncoming car approaches?
options: Immediately switch to dipped beam as soon as the oncoming vehicle can be dazzled
Leave the high beams on when the street is unlit
Flash the high beams briefly and leave them on
Switch to parking lights only
rule-grootlicht-tegenligger.explanation: According to Article 31.1, high beams must be extinguished and replaced by dipped beams as soon as an oncoming vehicle approaches to avoid dazzling.

rule-inhalen-kruispunt.question: Are you allowed to overtake another car on the left at an intersection where priority from the right applies?
options: Yes, as long as you don't drive faster than 50 km/h
No, overtaking a system of vehicles or a car on the left is prohibited at an intersection with priority from the right
Yes, but only if the intersection is clearly visible
Only if you use your horn
rule-inhalen-kruispunt.explanation: Article 17.2, 2°a prohibits overtaking a team or a motor vehicle with more than two wheels on the left at intersections where priority applies from the right.

rule-inhalen-oversteekplaats.question: Are you allowed to overtake a vehicle that slows down or stops at a zebra crossing without traffic lights?
options: Yes, provided you swerve to the left
Yes, if you don't see any pedestrians walking
No, it is strictly forbidden to overtake a vehicle approaching or stopping in front of a crossing
Only if you drive past at walking pace
rule-inhalen-oversteekplaats.explanation: Article 17.2, 5° prohibits overtaking a driver who stops in front of or approaches a pedestrian or cyclist crossing.

rule-snelheid-woonerf.question: What maximum speed applies within a residential area or a property?
options: 30 km/h
10 km/h
15 km/h
20 km/h
rule-snelheid-woonerf.explanation: According to Article 22bis, 3°, the speed in a yard or residential area may not exceed 20 km/h for all drivers.

rule-woonerf-voetganger.question: What special rule applies to pedestrians and children playing within a yard or residential area?
options: They may use the entire width of the public road and play there, without unnecessarily obstructing traffic
They must remain on the sidewalk
Children are only allowed to play in the street under the supervision of an adult
Pedestrians must always give way to approaching cars
rule-woonerf-voetganger.explanation: According to article 22bis.1°, pedestrians may use the entire width of the public road and playing is permitted. Drivers must not endanger them.

rule-slepen-snelheid.question: What is the maximum speed when a car tows another defective vehicle using a cable or tow bar?
options: 40 km/h
25 km/h
30 km/h
50 km/h
rule-slepen-snelheid.explanation: According to Article 49.1, the speed of a towed vehicle may never exceed 25 km/h during temporary towing with a cable or rod.

rule-alcohol-alarmfase.question: What immediate measure does the police impose in the event of a breath test with an 'Alarm' result (between 0.5 and 0.8 per mille)?
options: An immediate driving ban of 1 hour
Only a written warning without a driving ban
A temporary driving ban of 3 hours with suspension of the driver's license
A permanent revocation of the driver's license by the court
rule-alcohol-alarmfase.explanation: In the event of a breath test in the alarm phase (between 0.22 mg/l and 0.35 mg/l of exhaled air, or 0.5 and 0.8 per mille), an immediate temporary driving ban of 3 hours applies (Road Traffic Act art. 60).

rule-alcohol-positief-3uur.question: How long does the temporary driving ban imposed by the police last for a 'Positive' result from 0.8 per mille alcohol in the blood?
options: Minstens 2 uur
Minstens 4 uur
Minstens 12 uur
Minstens 6 uur
rule-alcohol-positief-3uur.explanation: From 0.35 mg/l exhaled alveolar air (0.8 per mille in the blood), the police imposes an immediate driving ban of at least 6 hours (Road Traffic Act art. 60).

rule-autosnelweg-omkeren.question: Are you allowed to turn around or reverse on a motorway if you have missed the exit?
options: No, turning, reversing and driving over the central reservation are strictly prohibited on the motorway
Yes, if you stay on the emergency lane and turn on four indicators
Yes, as long as you don't drive backwards faster than 10 km/h
Only if the police direct traffic
rule-autosnelweg-omkeren.explanation: According to Article 21.4, it is absolutely forbidden to make turns, reverse or use the central reservation on motorways.

rule-autosnelweg-pechstrook.question: When can you use the emergency lane on a motorway with a vehicle?
options: To make a phone call or take a rest
Only in case of breakdown or acute emergency, or when a dynamic traffic sign explicitly allows this
To drive past a traffic jam on the right to the nearest exit
When the other lanes are overcrowded
rule-autosnelweg-pechstrook.explanation: According to Articles 9.7 and 21.4, the emergency lane / emergency lane is exclusively intended for vehicles that are forced to stop due to breakdown or emergency, or as a rush-hour lane when indicated.

rule-autosnelweg-inhalen-rechts.question: When are you allowed to overtake another car on the right on a motorway?
options: When the left lane is traveling at a speed of less than 100 km/h
When you are in a hurry and the driver on the left does not want to move to the right
When traffic is in parallel traffic jams and your lane moves faster than the lane to your left
Overtaking on the right is strictly prohibited under all conceivable circumstances
rule-autosnelweg-inhalen-rechts.explanation: According to Article 16.2, passing vehicles in parallel traffic jams does not count as overtaking. In normal flowing traffic, overtaking on the right is always prohibited.

rule-rotonde-pinker.question: When should you turn on your right turn signal at a roundabout?
options: Well before you enter the roundabout
Constantly as long as you continue to drive on the roundabout
Only if there is a cyclist riding next to you
When you leave the roundabout, do so in time before your chosen exit
rule-rotonde-pinker.explanation: You do not have to blink when entering a roundabout. According to Article 19.2, 1°, you are obliged to use your right turn signal as soon as you leave the roundabout.

rule-rotonde-voorsorteren.question: Which lane do you prefer to choose on a multi-lane roundabout if you want to take the first exit?
options: The leftmost inner lane
The middle lane
That doesn't make any legal difference
The rightmost lane
rule-rotonde-voorsorteren.explanation: According to the general rule (art. 9.1.1) you must drive as close as possible to the right edge of the roadway. Those who leave the roundabout quickly (first exit) choose the right lane.

rule-schoolbus-gevaarslichten.question: What should you do if a school bus is stationary and its four direction indicators (hazard lights) and the 'transport of children' sign are on?
options: Sound the horn to warn children crossing the road
Just keep driving; the warning signal only applies to the bus passengers themselves
Turn around immediately and choose another route
Reduce your speed significantly and stop if necessary to ensure the safety of children
rule-schoolbus-gevaarslichten.explanation: Article 39bis stipulates that drivers must significantly reduce their speed and, if necessary, stop when a school transport bus is stationary with the hazard lights switched on.

rule-fietser-naast-elkaar.question: Are two cyclists allowed to ride next to each other on the road outside built-up areas?
options: No, outside built-up areas cyclists must always ride one behind the other
Yes, cyclists are allowed to ride with a maximum of four people next to each other anytime and anywhere
Only if the road is wider than 7 meters
Yes, but they have to drive one behind the other as soon as a vehicle from behind approaches
rule-fietser-naast-elkaar.explanation: According to Article 43.1, cyclists are allowed to ride two abreast, but outside built-up areas they must ride one behind the other when a vehicle approaching from behind is approaching.

sit-01-b5-stop.question: You cycle to school and come to this intersection with a STOP sign. Should you stop here?
options: No, as a cyclist I just have to slow down a little.
Yes, I must come to a complete stop and give priority to traffic from the left and right.
No, a STOP sign only applies to motorized vehicles.
sit-01-b5-stop.explanation: A STOP sign (B5) obliges every driver (including cyclists) to stop completely at the stop line and to give priority to drivers on the cross road.

sit-02-b17-voorrang-rechts.question: You arrive at this intersection with traffic sign B17. What should you do?
options: I make a mandatory stop and give priority to drivers from the left and right.
I can just drive on because sign B17 gives me priority.
I slow down and give priority to drivers coming from the right.
sit-02-b17-voorrang-rechts.explanation: Traffic sign B17 indicates that you are approaching an intersection where general right-of-way priority applies (art. 12.3.1).

sit-03-b1-haaientanden.question: You arrive by bike at this intersection with sign B1 and shark teeth. What should you do?
options: I slow down and give priority to drivers on the cross road (from left and right).
I am always obliged to stop with one foot on the ground, even when there is no traffic approaching.
I can drive quietly, because shark teeth only apply to motorists.
sit-03-b1-haaientanden.explanation: Traffic sign B1 (inverted triangle) and shark teeth oblige you to give priority to drivers on the cross road. You should only stop if necessary.

sit-04-b22-rechtsaf-rood.question: The traffic light is red, but there is sign B22 (yellow bicycle with arrow) on the pole. Are you allowed to turn right?
options: Yes, but only if there is no pedestrian crossing at all.
Yes, you may turn right at the red light provided you give priority to other road users.
No, at a red light you always have to wait until it turns green.
sit-04-b22-rechtsaf-rood.explanation: Traffic sign B22 allows cyclists to carefully turn right through the red or orange-yellow light, provided they give priority to other road users.

sit-05-f49-zebrapad-fietser.question: A pedestrian crosses the zebra crossing and a cyclist approaches. Who should give priority?
options: The pedestrian must stop for the cyclist.
The cyclist must only give way if the pedestrian has already passed half the zebra crossing.
The cyclist must give way to the crossing pedestrian.
sit-05-f49-zebrapad-fietser.explanation: Drivers (including cyclists) must give priority to pedestrians who are at or about to enter a crossing (art. 40.4.1).

sit-06-b19-smalle-doorgang.question: You approach this narrow passage with traffic sign B19. Who gets to drive through first?
options: The driver from the opposite direction may drive through first.
You can drive through first because cyclists always have priority at a narrowing.
The tallest or fastest driver may drive through first.
sit-06-b19-smalle-doorgang.explanation: Sign B19 prohibits driving into the passageway if it is not possible to cross without the oncoming traffic having to stop. The oncoming vehicle has sign B21 and goes first.

sit-07-kruispunt-drie-fietsers.question: Three cyclists arrive at this equivalent intersection simultaneously. Who gets to drive through first?
options: Cyclist 2, because he is riding straight ahead.
Cyclist 1, because he has priority from the right and has no traffic from the right.
Cyclist 3, because he is riding closest to the middle of the road.
sit-07-kruispunt-drie-fietsers.explanation: Without priority signs, priority applies from the right. Cyclist 3 must give way to cyclist 2, who must give way to cyclist 1. Cyclist 1 has no traffic from the right and goes first.

sit-08-licht-boven-bord.question: The traffic light is green, but there is also a STOP sign on the pole. What should you do?
options: First stop at the STOP sign, and then continue driving when it is still green.
Stop and give way to crossing traffic from the right.
Continue without stopping, because working traffic lights take precedence over traffic signs.
sit-08-licht-boven-bord.explanation: According to Article 6.3 of the Highway Code, the priority signs on the same road no longer apply as soon as the traffic lights are operational.

sit-09-fietszone-f111.question: You are riding in this bicycle street (cycling zone, sign F111). What rule applies here for motorists?
options: Motor vehicles are not allowed to overtake cyclists and the speed limit is 30 km/h.
Motor vehicles may always overtake cyclists provided they keep a minimum distance of 1 meter to the side.
Motor vehicles are not allowed to drive at all in a cycling zone.
sit-09-fietszone-f111.explanation: In a cycling zone (sign F111), motor vehicles are not allowed to overtake cyclists and a maximum speed of 30 km/h applies everywhere (art. 22novies).

sit-10-politieagent-halt.question: The police officer stands crosswise with his arms stretched horizontally at the intersection. What does this order mean?
options: Continue if you want to turn right.
Stop for all road users approaching the officer from the front or behind.
Stopping only for motorized vehicles, not for cyclists or pedestrians.
sit-10-politieagent-halt.explanation: The horizontally extended arms of an authorized person mean 'stop' for all road users approaching from directions that cross the officer's chest or back (art. 4.1).

sit-11-plaats-geen-fietspad.question: There is no cycle path on this road, only a footpath. Where should you ride as a cyclist (10 years and older)?
options: Right on the road.
On the sidewalk, as long as there are no pedestrians walking.
Left on the road against traffic to see cars approaching.
sit-11-plaats-geen-fietspad.explanation: If there is no cycle path, cyclists (10 years and older) must ride on the right of the road. The footpath is reserved for pedestrians (art. 9.1.2).

sit-12-step-trottoir.question: You ride a non-motorized scooter on public roads. Where should you drive?
options: Always mandatory on the road between the cars.
That depends on your speed: at walking pace you follow the rules for pedestrians, faster those for cyclists.
Always on the cycle path, regardless of speed.
sit-12-step-trottoir.explanation: Users of non-motorized propulsion devices follow the rules for pedestrians as long as they do not travel faster than walking pace. If they drive faster, the rules for cyclists apply (art. 7bis).

sit-13-bebouwde-kom-naast-elkaar.question: Two cyclists ride next to each other in a built-up area and a car approaches behind them. What should cyclists do?
options: They must immediately drive one after the other.
They must stop and stand on the side of the road.
They may continue to drive next to each other, as long as crossing with oncoming traffic remains possible.
sit-13-bebouwde-kom-naast-elkaar.explanation: Within built-up areas, cyclists are allowed to ride two abreast. They must only drive one behind the other when crossing with an oncoming vehicle is otherwise not possible (art. 43.2).

sit-14-fietspad-d7-enkelrichting.question: Are you allowed to cycle in the opposite direction on this cycle path indicated by sign D7?
options: No, a cycle path may only be used in the direction of travel in which the D7 sign is visible.
Yes, you can always cycle in both directions on a cycle path.
Yes, but only if you live within a radius of 500 meters.
sit-14-fietspad-d7-enkelrichting.explanation: A cycle path indicated with sign D7 may only be used in the direction in which the sign is visible, unless an undersign or road marking indicates that it is a two-way cycle path (art. 9.1.2.1°).

sit-15-kind-voetpad.question: Until what age are children allowed to ride a bicycle on the sidewalk?
options: Up to 6 years.
Up to 10 years, provided they do not endanger pedestrians.
Children are never allowed to cycle on the sidewalk.
sit-15-kind-voetpad.explanation: Children under the age of 10 may ride their bicycle on the sidewalk or raised verge, provided they do not endanger other road users (art. 9.1.2.3°, increased from 9 to 10 years in 2022).

sit-16-voetganger-links-rijbaan.question: There is no sidewalk, verge or cycle path. On which side should pedestrians step onto the roadway?
options: On the right, in the same direction as motorized traffic.
Pedestrians should never walk on the roadway if there is no sidewalk.
On the left side of the road, so that they can clearly see oncoming traffic approaching.
sit-16-voetganger-links-rijbaan.explanation: When pedestrians have to use the road due to the lack of a sidewalk, accessible shoulder or cycle path, they must step to the left of the road compared to their walking direction (art. 42.2.1°).

sit-17-b9-voorrangsweg.question: You are driving on this road with traffic sign B9 (orange/yellow diamond). What priority rule applies here?
options: Drivers from side streets must give you priority; you are driving on a priority road.
Right-hand priority still applies at every intersection.
This sign only indicates the end of the built-up area.
sit-17-b9-voorrangsweg.explanation: Traffic sign B9 indicates that you are driving on a priority road. Drivers coming from side roads must give way to drivers on the main road (art. 67.3).

sit-18-b21-voorrang-tegenliggers.question: You approach this narrow passage with traffic sign B21 (blue square with white and red arrow). Who gets to drive through first?
options: The oncoming vehicle can always drive through first.
You can drive through first; oncoming traffic must give way.
The largest car always goes first.
sit-18-b21-voorrang-tegenliggers.explanation: Traffic sign B21 indicates that drivers have priority over oncoming drivers in a narrow passage (art. 67.4).

sit-19-f19-beperkt-eenrichting.question: You cycle to this street with sign F19 and bottom sign M2 (bicycle with arrows). What does this mean?
options: Cyclists may enter this one-way street in both directions (limited one-way traffic).
Cyclists are only allowed to ride here between 9am and 5pm.
Cyclists must dismount and continue on foot.
sit-19-f19-beperkt-eenrichting.explanation: Sign F19 with subsign M2 indicates a street with limited one-way traffic (SUL): motorized traffic may only drive in one direction, but cyclists may ride in both directions (art. 65.2 & art. 71).

sit-20-f4a-zone-30.question: You drive past traffic sign F4a (zone 30). What speed limit applies from here?
options: The speed limit is 50 km/h, except on school streets.
The maximum speed is 30 km/h in the entire zone up to the zone end sign.
The speed limit only applies during school hours.
sit-20-f4a-zone-30.explanation: Traffic sign F4a indicates the start of a zone in which the speed is limited everywhere to a maximum of 30 km/h, until sign F4b indicates the end of the zone (art. 71 & art. 22quater).

sit-21-rotonde-voorrang.question: You approach this roundabout indicated by signs D5 and B1 with shark teeth. Who has priority?
options: Drivers already driving on the roundabout have priority over oncoming traffic.
As the driving driver, you have priority from the right at the roundabout.
Whoever drives fastest always has priority.
sit-21-rotonde-voorrang.explanation: When entering a roundabout (sign D5 in combination with B1 and shark teeth), you must give priority to all drivers already driving on the roundabout (art. 12.3.1 and art. 67.2).

sit-22-overweg-slagbomen.question: The red lights flash and the railway crossing barriers go down. What should you do?
options: Cross quickly as long as the barrier is not completely closed.
Stop immediately at the stop line or traffic light and wait until the lights go out and the barriers are fully open.
Sound the horn to warn the train driver that you want to pass.
sit-22-overweg-slagbomen.explanation: As soon as the red lights flash or the barriers start moving, it is prohibited to drive onto the level crossing. Drivers are obliged to stop (art. 20.3, 2°).

sit-23-voorsorteren-pijlen.question: You are driving in the lane with the arrow pointing to the left. Are you allowed to drive straight ahead at the intersection?
options: Yes, if there is no other traffic driving next to you at that moment.
Yes, as long as you turn on your right turn signal.
No, pre-sorting arrows on the road surface require you to follow the indicated direction.
sit-23-voorsorteren-pijlen.explanation: Pre-sorting arrows placed on the roadway oblige drivers to follow the direction indicated by the arrows (art. 77.1).

sit-24-fietssuggestiestrook.question: You drive by car along this red-ochre colored bicycle suggestion lane (without traffic sign D7 or white broken line). Can you drive this?
options: Yes, a bicycle lane is an integral part of the roadway; cars may drive on it, but may not endanger or hinder cyclists.
No, a bicycle lane is exclusively reserved for cyclists and prohibited for cars.
Only if you drive faster than 50 km/h.
sit-24-fietssuggestiestrook.explanation: A bicycle lane is not a real bicycle path and does not have the legal status of a reserved section: it is part of the roadway over which cars are allowed to drive without hindering cyclists (art. 2.62 & art. 9.1.2).

sit-25-erf-woonerf-f12a.question: You enter a street with traffic sign F12a (yard/residential area). What rule applies here for pedestrians and speed?
options: The speed limit is 30 km/h and pedestrians must stay on the sidewalk.
The speed limit is 20 km/h and pedestrians are allowed to use and play on the full width of the public road.
Motor vehicles are prohibited here at all times.
sit-25-erf-woonerf-f12a.explanation: Within a yard or residential area (sign F12a), a maximum speed of 20 km/h applies and pedestrians may use the entire width of the public road (art. 22bis).

sit-26-prioritair-voertuig.question: An ambulance is approaching behind you with blue flashing lights and the special sound device (siren) switched on. What should you do?
options: Just keep your speed; the vehicle will overtake you automatically.
Immediately brake hard and stop in the middle of the road.
Immediately clear the passage, slow down and, if necessary, stop or swerve to give way.
sit-26-prioritair-voertuig.explanation: As soon as a priority vehicle uses its blue flashing lights and siren, every road user must immediately clear the passage and give way (art. 38).

sit-27-doorlopende-witte-streep.question: You are driving behind this slow tractor on a road with a continuous white line. Can you overtake the tractor by crossing the line?
options: No, it is strictly forbidden to drive over or cross a solid white line, not even to overtake a slow vehicle.
Yes, you can always overtake agricultural vehicles and tractors across a continuous line.
Yes, as long as you don't drive faster than 30 km/h.
sit-27-doorlopende-witte-streep.explanation: A continuous white line may under no circumstances be crossed (art. 72.2). Overtaking by driving over the solid line is prohibited, even with a slow tractor.

sit-28-parkeren-trottoir-verbod.question: Are you allowed to park your car with two wheels on the sidewalk as shown in this photo, if there is no traffic sign E9b?
options: Yes, as long as there is at least 1 meter of space for pedestrians.
No, parking on the sidewalk is prohibited unless a specific traffic sign (such as E9b) expressly allows this.
Yes, but only at night and during weekends.
sit-28-parkeren-trottoir-verbod.explanation: Standing still and parking on the sidewalk is prohibited according to Article 24.1°, unless sign E9b explicitly allows this (Article 23.1 and Article 70).

sit-29-busstrook-f17.question: You drive a normal passenger car. Are you allowed to drive on this special roadbed or bus lane (sign F17 and marking 'BUS')?
options: Yes, if there is no bus in sight at that moment.
Yes, to overtake a line of cars on the right.
No, regular cars are only allowed to drive in the immediate vicinity of an intersection to change directions.
sit-29-busstrook-f17.explanation: A bus lane or special road surface (sign F17) is reserved for public transport. Other drivers may only drive the last few meters to turn at an intersection (art. 72.5).

sit-30-blindengeleidehond-oversteken.question: A person with a white cane or guide dog wants to cross. What should you do as an approaching driver?
options: Give way and in all circumstances yield and stop to allow the person to cross safely.
Briefly honk the horn to let us know that you are passing by.
Only stop if the person is already in the middle of the road.
sit-30-blindengeleidehond-oversteken.explanation: Drivers must in all circumstances give way and stop for blind people with a white cane or persons with a guide dog who are on the roadway (art. 40.2).

sit-31-rechtsaf-fietser-voorrang.question: You want to turn right by car at this intersection while a cyclist continues straight on the cycle path. Who has priority?
options: The car, because turning right is a shorter turn.
The cyclist who continues straight on the same road has priority over the turning car.
Whoever reaches the intersection first has priority.
sit-31-rechtsaf-fietser-voorrang.explanation: A driver who changes direction (turning right) must give priority to other road users (such as cyclists) who continue to drive straight on the same public road (art. 19.3.2°).

sit-32-knipperlicht-beweegbare-brug.question: You approach this movable bridge where two red lights flash alternately. What does this signal mean?
options: The bridge is open to shipping; it is forbidden to drive past the stop signal.
You can continue driving if you don't see a boat sailing.
The signal only applies to trucks heavier than 3.5 tons.
sit-32-knipperlicht-beweegbare-brug.explanation: Two alternately flashing red lights at a movable bridge mean 'prohibition on driving past the stop line or traffic light' (art. 64.1).

sit-33-geel-knipperlicht-kruispunt.question: The traffic lights at this intersection are flashing orange-yellow and there are no priority signs. Which priority rule applies?
options: Drivers on the widest road always automatically have priority.
The general right-of-way priority applies to the intersection.
Everyone must come to a complete stop for 5 seconds.
sit-33-geel-knipperlicht-kruispunt.explanation: When traffic lights flash orange-yellow and there are no priority signs, the normal priority rules apply, namely the priority from the right (art. 6.3 & art. 12.3.1).

sit-34-fietsopstelvak-f107.question: Where should motorists stop at a red traffic light with a bicycle parking space (OFOS, sign F107) on the roadway?
options: In the middle of the green bicycle parking area.
At the second stop line just before the traffic lights.
Before the first stop line, so that the line-up area remains completely free for cyclists and two-wheelers.
sit-34-fietsopstelvak-f107.explanation: Motorists must stop before the first stop line. The space between the two stop lines (the bicycle parking area, sign F107) is reserved for cyclists and two-wheeled moped riders (art. 77.8).

sit-35-schoolstraat-c3.question: What does sign C3 with the sign 'Schoolstraat' mean at the beginning of this street during the indicated hours?
options: The street is closed to all motor vehicles during school start and end hours.
Cars are only allowed to drive there if they turn on their four hazard lights.
Parents who take their children to school by car are always allowed to drive through.
sit-35-schoolstraat-c3.explanation: In a school street (art. 2.68 and art. 22decies), the public road is closed to motor vehicles during certain hours. Only pedestrians, cyclists and emergency services are allowed through.

sit-36-spitsstrook-matrixbord.question: A green arrow pointing downwards lights up on the matrix board above the emergency lane/rush-hour lane. Are you allowed to drive on this lane?
options: No, the hard shoulder may never be used for driving.
Yes, the green arrow indicates that the rush hour lane is open as an extra lane.
Only if you maintain a speed of at least 130 km/h.
sit-36-spitsstrook-matrixbord.explanation: When the dynamic lane signaling shows a green arrow above the rush-hour lane, it may be used as a full-fledged lane (art. 9.7 & art. 65.4).

sit-37-tram-halte-uitstappen.question: A tram stops on the carriageway at a stop without a raised platform and passengers get off. What should you do as a following driver?
options: Drive quickly around the tram on the left.
Sound the horn so that the travelers move aside.
Stop at the entry and exit sides to allow travelers to safely reach the roadway or sidewalk.
sit-37-tram-halte-uitstappen.explanation: When a tram stops without a raised platform, drivers must stop on the boarding and alighting side to allow passengers to cross safely (art. 40.1).

sit-38-bevoegd-persoon-arm-omhoog.question: A police officer stands at the intersection with one arm raised vertically. What does this order mean?
options: Stop for all road users from all directions, except those already at the intersection.
Stopping only for cyclists and pedestrians.
Traffic is allowed to move at a faster pace.
sit-38-bevoegd-persoon-arm-omhoog.explanation: A vertically raised arm of an authorized person means 'attention and stop' for all road users from all directions, except those already at the intersection (art. 4.1).

sit-39-afstand-inhalen-fietser.question: What minimum lateral distance must a car maintain when overtaking a cyclist outside built-up areas?
options: At least 0.5 meters.
At least 1.5 meters.
At least 1 meter.
sit-39-afstand-inhalen-fietser.explanation: Outside built-up areas, a driver must leave a lateral space of at least 1.5 meters when overtaking a cyclist or pedestrian (within built-up areas this is at least 1 meter, art. 40ter).

sit-40-reddingsstrook-file.question: There is a traffic jam on a two-lane highway. How should drivers form a rescue lane?
options: All vehicles must move to the emergency lane.
Everyone just stays in the middle of their lane.
Vehicles in the left lane swerve as much as possible to the left, vehicles in the right lane as much as possible to the right.
sit-40-reddingsstrook-file.explanation: In the event of traffic jams, vehicles in the left lane must drive on the far left and those in the right lane must drive on the far right to leave a free rescue lane in the middle for emergency services (art. 2.70 & art. 9.8).

sit-41-c31b-rechtsaf-verboden-fietsers.question: You approach this intersection in Antwerp with sign C31b and a bottom sign 'EXCEPT' with a bicycle symbol. Are you allowed to turn right here by car?
options: No, no one is allowed to turn right here, not even cyclists.
Yes, the ban only applies at night.
No, the ban applies to cars, but cyclists are exempt and are allowed to turn right.
sit-41-c31b-rechtsaf-verboden-fietsers.explanation: Sign C31b prohibits turning right at the intersection (art. 68 KB 1 December 1975). The 'EXCEPT' sign with bicycle symbol limits this ban to motorized traffic; cyclists are allowed to turn right.

sit-42-e9a-gehandicaptenparkeerplaats.question: You see this parking sign in a parking lot. Who is allowed to park here?
options: Only vehicles with a valid European disabled parking card.
Everyone, as long as the parking disc is used.
Taxis and delivery vehicles only.
sit-42-e9a-gehandicaptenparkeerplaats.explanation: Sign E9a with wheelchair symbol indicates a parking space reserved exclusively for vehicles used by persons with disabilities and a valid parking card (art. 70.2.1).

sit-43-hoogte-gewicht-brug-bus-uitzonder.question: You approach this bridge with signs for a height restriction of 3.80 m and a weight restriction of 10 tons, with the bottom sign 'Excepte bus et autocars'. Is a 14-ton scheduled bus allowed to cross here?
options: Yes, because the sign expressly excludes buses and coaches from the weight restriction.
Only if the bus is less than 3.80 m high, but the weight remains prohibited.
No, the weight ban applies to all vehicles without exception.
sit-43-hoogte-gewicht-brug-bus-uitzonder.explanation: Signs C29 (height) and C21 (mass) prohibit access above the indicated values ​​(art. 68), but the bottom sign 'Excepte bus et autocars' expressly excludes scheduled buses and coaches from both prohibition signs.

sit-44-f103-voetgangerszone-laden-lossen.question: You drive a van to this street with sign F103 and the bottom sign 'Except loading and unloading from 6:30 PM to 11:30 AM'. Are you allowed to drive in here at 9am to deliver?
options: No, a pedestrian zone is prohibited for vehicles at any time.
Yes, because 9 am falls within the time period in which loading and unloading is permitted.
Yes, but only if you use a bicycle instead of a van.
sit-44-f103-voetgangerszone-laden-lossen.explanation: Sign F103 indicates the beginning of a pedestrian zone, where vehicles are in principle not allowed to drive (art. 71.2). The bottom sign allows loading and unloading between 6:30 PM and 11:30 AM, so 9 AM falls within that exception.

sit-45-c1-eenrichting-fietsers-bromfiets.question: This street in Antwerp has sign C1 with a bottom sign 'EXCEPT' for cyclists and mopeds class A. Are you allowed to drive here with a moped class A, against the direction of other traffic?
options: No, sign C1 prohibits this for all drivers without exception.
Only if you get off the moped and lead them by the hand.
Yes, the sign expressly excludes cyclists and class A mopeds from the ban.
sit-45-c1-eenrichting-fietsers-bromfiets.explanation: Sign C1 basically prohibits anyone from driving in that direction. A sign with a bicycle and moped symbol can exempt cyclists and class A mopeds from that ban, such as on a street with limited one-way traffic (art. 65.2).

sit-46-c3-verboden-toegang-beide-richtin.question: At the entrance to the Market in Maaseik you will see this completely red sign. Can you drive here by car?
options: No, sign C3 closes the road to all drivers in both directions.
Yes, as long as you drive at walking pace.
Yes, but only for parking.
sit-46-c3-verboden-toegang-beide-richtin.explanation: The completely red sign C3 prohibits access, in both directions, for any driver (art. 68 KB 1 December 1975); only pedestrians and any explicitly excluded categories are still allowed.

sit-47-c31a-links-afslaan-verboden.question: You want to turn left at this intersection, but you see this sign hanging on the facade. Is that allowed?
options: Yes, the ban only applies to trucks.
No, sign C31a prohibits turning in the direction of the arrow at the intersection, here on the left.
Yes, turning left is always allowed when there is no traffic approaching.
sit-47-c31a-links-afslaan-verboden.explanation: Sign C31a prohibits drivers from turning at the next intersection in the direction indicated by the arrow, here to the left (art. 68 KB 1 December 1975).

sit-48-a45-overweg-enkel-spoor-zonder-sl.question: You are approaching this railway crossing along the Maas. There are no barriers, only a St. Andrew's cross. What should you pay attention to?
options: Without barriers there is no danger, you can just drive through.
You have to judge for yourself whether a train is coming and stop as soon as it approaches or the lights flash.
You must always stop completely here, even if there is clearly no train in sight.
sit-48-a45-overweg-enkel-spoor-zonder-sl.explanation: Sign A45 indicates a single track level crossing (art. 66). Without barriers, you have to be careful: stop as soon as a train approaches or the flashing lights come on, and only cross when it is safe (art. 20.3).

sit-49-d10-voetgangers-fietserspad.question: You cycle along the Maas in Liège on this path with sign D10. Can a class A moped also drive here?
options: Yes, sign D10 allows pedestrians, cyclists and class A mopeds.
Yes, but only class A mopeds, not regular cyclists.
No, unlike sign D9, class A mopeds are not allowed to drive on a D10 path.
sit-49-d10-voetgangers-fietserspad.explanation: Sign D10 indicates a path reserved for pedestrians and cyclists; In contrast to sign D9, class A mopeds are not allowed to drive here (art. 69.3).

sit-50-a23-schoolomgeving-zone30.question: Here you drive past a school area with a warning sign for children and a 30 km/h zone sign. What does this mean for your speed?
options: You must drive a maximum of 30 km/h here, over the entire zone and not just at the sign.
Only at the blackboard itself the speed limit is 30 km/h, after which you can go faster again.
The speed limit only applies during school hours.
sit-50-a23-schoolomgeving-zone30.explanation: The warning sign announces a place where many children may appear (art. 66); the zone sign F4a imposes a maximum speed of 30 km/h for the entire zone, until the sign F4b lifts this limit again (art. 71 & art. 22quater).

sit-51-a31-matrixbord-wegenwerken-file.question: On the motorway you see this electronic matrix sign: 'Working in Ghent-Seaport, traffic jam from Oostakker'. What do you do with this?
options: You ignore the sign, because electronic signs are not binding.
You anticipate delays, reduce your speed in time and take into account traffic jams further down the road.
You must immediately stop on the road until the traffic jam has cleared.
sit-51-a31-matrixbord-wegenwerken-file.explanation: A variable information sign, just like a fixed A31 sign, warns of works and danger on the road ahead (art. 66); Drivers must adjust their speed in time and anticipate announced traffic disruptions.

sit-52-a5-steile-helling-kemmelberg.question: You are cycling or driving onto Kemmelbergstraat and see this sign. What does it warn about?
options: For a steep slope (climbing section of road).
Before a dangerous bend to the left.
For uneven road surfaces.
sit-52-a5-steile-helling-kemmelberg.explanation: Traffic sign A5 warns of a steep slope, such as here on the climb of the Kemmelberg in Heuvelland (art. 66 KB 1 December 1975).

sit-53-a13-oneffen-wegdek-vooraankondigi.question: You see this sign marked '150 m' along a rural road. What can you expect 150 meters away?
options: A transverse dip, a donkey's ridge or another uneven road surface.
A mandatory stop with priority from the right.
The end of the public road.
sit-53-a13-oneffen-wegdek-vooraankondigi.explanation: Traffic sign A13 warns of a cross-cut, a donkey's back or an uneven road surface; the bottom sign '150 m' indicates the distance to that hazard (art. 66 KB 1 December 1975).

sit-54-a39-einde-eenrichtingsverkeer.question: You're driving on a road at night and see these two triangles with a down arrow and an up arrow. What do they mean?
options: That you are obliged to turn around.
That one-way traffic ends and traffic is allowed in both directions again.
That oncoming traffic is given priority in a narrow passage.
sit-54-a39-einde-eenrichtingsverkeer.explanation: Traffic sign A39 warns that one-way traffic ends and that traffic is allowed in both directions again; so pay attention again to oncoming traffic (art. 66 KB of December 1, 1975).

sit-55-d3-verplichte-rijrichting-pijl.question: At this intersection you will see a blue round sign with an arrow pointing straight ahead and to the left. Which directions can you follow?
options: Just straight ahead.
Left only.
Straight ahead or left, you choose which of the two directions indicated.
sit-55-d3-verplichte-rijrichting-pijl.explanation: Sign D3 obliges drivers to follow one of the directions indicated by the arrows, here straight ahead or left; you can choose between the indicated directions, but not turn right (art. 69 KB 1 December 1975).

rule-gevarendriehoek-afstand.question: At what distance must you place a warning triangle in case of a breakdown on a motorway?
options: At least 50 meters behind your vehicle
At least 30 meters ahead of your vehicle
Right next to your vehicle, within 5 meters
At least 100 meters ahead of your vehicle
rule-gevarendriehoek-afstand.explanation: In case of a breakdown or accident, place the warning triangle facing oncoming traffic: at least 30 meters on a normal road, at least 100 meters ahead of your vehicle on a motorway.

rule-veiligheidsvest.question: When must the driver of a car wear a reflective safety vest?
options: Only at night, regardless of the situation
A safety vest is never mandatory in Belgium, only recommended
In case of a breakdown or accident, as soon as he steps out of the vehicle
Only when passengers are on board
rule-veiligheidsvest.explanation: In case of a breakdown or accident, the driver must wear a retro-reflective safety vest as soon as they leave the vehicle; this is not mandatory for passengers, though recommended.

rule-volgafstand.question: What is the rule of thumb for a safe following distance on roads where more than 50 km/h is allowed?
options: At least 1 car length, regardless of speed
At least 2 seconds of following time behind the car ahead
There is no general rule of thumb, only a ban on tailgating
At least 5 seconds of following time, always
rule-volgafstand.explanation: On roads with a speed limit above 50 km/h, the 'two-second rule' is the rule of thumb for a safe following distance; on wet roads, 3 seconds is safer.

rule-aanhangwagen-code96.question: With a category B license and code 96, you may tow a trailer with an MTM above 750 kg. Up to what maximum combined weight (towing vehicle + trailer)?
rule-aanhangwagen-code96.explanation: With category B alone, a trailer up to 750 kg MTM is allowed; with code 96, the trailer may be heavier, as long as the combined weight of towing vehicle and trailer does not exceed 4,250 kg.

rule-autokeuring-nieuwe-wagen.question: How many years after purchase must a new passenger car undergo its first periodic technical inspection?
options: 1 year
2 years
6 years
4 years
rule-autokeuring-nieuwe-wagen.explanation: A new passenger car only needs to be presented for its first technical inspection 4 years after purchase.

rule-rijbewijs-am-praktijk.question: From what age can you take the practical exam for the AM license, required to ride a moped up to 45 km/h?
options: 15 years
18 years
16 years
17 years
rule-rijbewijs-am-praktijk.explanation: The theory exam for the AM license can be taken from age 15 years and 9 months, but the practical exam only from age 16.

rule-drugs-nultolerantie.question: What is the legal rule for driving under the influence of illegal drugs in Belgium?
options: Only punishable for professional drivers
Zero tolerance: any trace of an illegal drug in a positive saliva test is punishable
Allowed as long as you are not clearly unfit to drive
Only punishable on a second offense within a year
rule-drugs-nultolerantie.explanation: Belgium applies a zero-tolerance policy for drugs in traffic: as soon as a saliva test shows a trace of an illegal drug, it is punishable, regardless of the amount.

rule-vluchtmisdrijf.question: What are you legally required to do if you are involved in a traffic accident?
options: Only stay if there are injuries, otherwise you may leave
You may leave as soon as you leave your details on a note
Only stay if you are at fault yourself
Stay at the scene so the necessary findings can be made
rule-vluchtmisdrijf.explanation: Anyone involved in an accident must stay at the scene so the findings can be made; leaving to avoid this is a hit-and-run offense (art. 33 §1 of the Traffic Act of 16 March 1968).

rule-lading-uitstekend.question: How far may cargo protrude behind your vehicle at most without mandatory extra signaling?
options: 1 meter
50 centimeters
3 meters
2 meters
rule-lading-uitstekend.explanation: Cargo may protrude at most 1 meter behind the vehicle without special signaling; for long indivisible items this may be up to 3 meters, but then a red-and-white warning board is mandatory.

rule-motorhelm.question: Who is required to wear a motorcycle helmet on a motorcycle over 50 cc?
options: Only the driver
Both the driver and the passenger
Only the passenger
No one, a bicycle helmet suffices for both
rule-motorhelm.explanation: Both the driver and the passenger of a motorcycle over 50 cc must wear an approved CE-labeled motorcycle helmet.
